Q: Set toolpath to MSBuild 2019 in a TFS 2013 using (XALM) build process templates A:

Continuous Integration in Team Foundation Build 2013 is designed to use VS2013 period Build Tools with NuGet 2.x.

The following caveats should be considered...

  • MSBuild 15.0 and newer are installed to a different directory than earlier build tools.

  • Full versions of Visual Studio do not need to be installed on the Build server, you can install Build Tools for VS2022 instead.

  • TF Build 2013 12.0 MSBuild Tools can be overridden with build arguments but default NuGet.exe paths are read-only.

  • If the Visual Studio solution uses a newer version of NuGet (it contains a packages.config) or contains modern dotnet projects, NuGet 7 CLI should be installed and configured manually and the default NuGet restore step should be disabled in the Build Definition by adding custom Build process parameters in "MSBuild arguments".

  • Instead, the NuGet package restore should be invoked as a Pre-build script (using a batch or powershell script).

Edit Build Definition for MSBuild 17 (VS2022 compatible)

  1. You can specify a newer version of NuGet with an existing TFS Build Process Template. Download the current NuGet CLI version - currently it is v7.6.

Use a suitable batch or powershell script, for example...

Either...

C:\vstools\nuget.exe restore "%TF_BUILD_SOURCESDIRECTORY%\solution.sln" ^
  -MSBuildPath "C:\YourDirectory\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools\MSBuild\Current\Bin" ^
  -NonInteractive ^
  -Verbosity normal

Or try...

C:\vstools\nuget.exe install "%TF_BUILD_SOURCESDIRECTORY%\packages.config" ^
  -OutputDirectory "%TF_BUILD_SOURCESDIRECTORY%\packages"

The script should be checked into source control.

  1. Edit the TFS "Build Definition" in Visual Studio and click the "Process" tab.

Reference previous script in the "Pre-build script path" in the Edit Build Definition - Build Process Template section.

For example $/Collection/BuildTemplates/pre-compile-example.bat

  1. Expand the "Advanced" Build process parameters and specify overridden MSBuild arguments inline as a single string of parameters (using spaces between each parameter and without line breaks).
/tv:17.0

/p:GenerateBuildInfoConfigFile=false 

/p:VisualStudioVersion=17.0 

/p:MSBuildExtensionsPath="C:\YourDirectory\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools\MSBuild" 

/p:ToolPath="C:\YourDirectory\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools\MSBuild\Current\Bin\Roslyn"  

/p:RoslynTargetsPath="C:\YourDirectory\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools\MSBuild\Current\Bin\Roslyn" 

/p:MsBuildPath="C:\YourDirectory\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools\MSBuild\Current\Bin\amd64" 

/p:NuGetTasksAssemblyPath="C:\YourDirectory\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools\Common7\IDE\CommonExtensions\Microsoft\NuGet\NuGet.Build.Tasks.dll" 

/p:CustomAfterMicrosoftCommonTargets="C:\YourDirectory\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools\Common7\IDE\CommonExtensions\Microsoft\NuGet\NuGet.targets" 

/p:RestorePackages=false 

/p:RestorePackagesConfig=false
  • If the previous hasn't worked, upgrade to a newer Build Definition Template e.g. TfvcTemplate.12.xaml in Visual Studio and append a ToolVersion attribute using a code editor like Notepad++ to avoid breaking the XAML. Then apply the same MSBuild arguments as mentioned earlier.
<mtba:RunMSBuild ...
ToolVersion="17.0" />

A simpler solution would be to upgrade from Team Foundation Server 2013 to at least Team Foundation Server 2015/2017 and it would recognise the revised MSBuild 15.0 and newer Build paths with the correct Build Tools installed.

Q: Right way to extend spring beans A:

In order to have multiple Beans of the same type or simultaneously have Beans extending each other, you need to give them a "name" (Qualifier) using the annotation @Qualifier both on the Bean definition and on the Autowired member.

Read about it here: Spring Bean Qualifiers

Q: "Error: no suitable method found for reduce" when reducing an int[] array using streams A:

The problem here is that var sum = Arrays.asList(nums) returns a List<int[]>, rather than a List of integer values. The result of sum.stream() is a Stream<int[]>, not a Stream<Integer> or an IntStream, so the arguments to the reduce method don't match the stream's type.

Explanation

The signature of Stream.reduce is T reduce(T identity, BinaryOperator<T> accumulator). Therefore, the reduce method of sum.stream() expects int[] as the type of the first argument, and a BinaryOperator<int[]> as the second argument. Since your first argument is the int 0 and not an int[], the compilation error occurs.

The reason Arrays.asList(nums) is returning a List<int[]> is that Arrays.asList takes in a vararg array of objects. int is a primitive, but the whole int[] array is an object. Therefore, the compiler is interpreting nums as the first and only varargs argument, rather than taking each element from the array.

Solutions

Using Arrays.stream will get an IntStream, which will work with your existing reduce method call:

int[] nums = { 1,3,4,5,7};
var sum= Arrays.stream(nums).reduce(0,(a,b)->a + b);

Alternatively, the built-in IntStream.sum method can be used in your specific case:

var result = Arrays.stream(nums).sum();

Q: How do I log the result of Copy-Item? A:

Copy-Item doesn't produce output when it succeeds unless you use -PassThru. If you want to log all PowerShell commands and their output, Start-Transcript is a simple solution.

Start-Transcript -Path ".\Logs\$date-start-Automation.txt" -Append
# Copy commands
Copy-Item C:\Windows\CMSLOGS\*.log -Destination C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\IntuneManagementExtension\Logs\CMSLOGS
Copy-Item C:\Windows\CMSLOGS\*.flg -Destination C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\IntuneManagementExtension\Logs\CMSLOGS
Stop-Transcript

Stop-Transcript is important because it closes the transcript and saves the log correctly. If you only need to log the copied files, another option is to use Copy-Item -PassThru.

Q: Trying to read CSV file , says "Error in nchar(x, "width") : invalid multibyte string, element 1" , how do fix this? A:

R recently returned a very similar error message (*) to me for a bunch of *.html files that rvest::read_html(x) has previously read into R without any problem.

(*)          “Error in nchar(x) : invalid multibyte string, element 1”

This unexpected error occurred directly after I upgraded to latest R-4.6.1 and ran Update Packages. In my case the correct encoding name for my *.html files was: "UTF-16LE". Though confusing at first, the problem was quickly identified by using helper function rvest::guess_encoding(x) which returns a list of best guess encoding names in order of confidence level. For my case "UTF-16LE" came 3rd on the guess list, all others failed to read my *.html files into R. See link for this excellent tidyverse helper function below:

https://rvest.tidyverse.org/reference/encoding.html

I’ve since successfully used rvest::guess_encoding(x) to help identify correct encoding names for reading into R *.html, *.htm, *.csv and *.txt files: 3 out of these 4 file types required different encoding names.
